content: 1. Efavirenz affects the metabolism of drugs processed by the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Exercise caution and monitor patients closely when co-administering efavirenz with such drugs. 2. For patients taking exemestane alongside a potent CYP3A4 inducer, the recommended dose of exemestane is 50 mg daily after a meal. 3. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Adjust the doses of drugs that are substrates of CYP3A4 as necessary when co-administered with efavirenz. 5. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of felbamate, felodipine, and fentanyl by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 6. Co-administration of fentanyl with CYP3A4 inducers may reduce fentanyl plasma concentrations, leading to reduced efficacy or withdrawal symptoms in physically dependent patients. Monitor therapy closely. 7. Both fentanyl and efavirenz increase sedation. Use caution and monitor patients. 8. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of fentanyl (intranasal, transdermal, transmucosal) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 9. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of fesoterodine and flibanserin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduce flibanserin systemic exposure. Use caution and monitor. 10. Efavirenz and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor. 11. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 12. Efavirenz and fluoxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 13. Efavirenz and fluphenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 14. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of flurazepam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 15. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of flurbiprofen and fluvastatin by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 16. Fluvoxamine increases efavirenz levels by affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 17. Efavirenz and formoterol both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 18. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir and fosaprepitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Efavirenz and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. Use caution and monitor. 20. Efavirenz and ganaxolone both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 21. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of gefitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Increase gefitinib to 500 mg daily if co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer, and resume the standard dose 7 days after discontinuing the inducer. Monitor closely. 22. Efavirenz and gemifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 23. Efavirenz and gilteritinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 24. Efavirenz and goserelin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 25. Efavirenz and granisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 26. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of guanfacine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduce guanfacine plasma concentrations and elimination half-life. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 27. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of haloperidol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 28. Efavirenz and histrelin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 29. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised when discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers co-administered with hydrocodone, as plasma concentrations may increase, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Monitor closely. 30. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone and hydroxyprogesterone caproate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Efavirenz and hydroxyzine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 32. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of ibuprofen (oral and IV) by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 33. Efavirenz increases the toxicity of ifosfamide by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. CYP3A4 inducers may increase the formation of neurotoxic/nephrotoxic metabolites like chloroacetaldehyde. Monitor for increased effects/toxicities. 34. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of iloperidone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone increases efavirenz levels. Use caution and monitor. 35. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of imipramine by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 36. Efavirenz and indacaterol both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 37. Indinavir and efavirenz both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 38. Isoniazid increases efavirenz levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 39. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of isosorbide dinitrate, isosorbide mononitrate, and isradipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Efavirenz and isradipine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 40. Istradefylline increases efavirenz levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Use caution and monitor. 41. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 42. Ivosidenib decreases efavirenz levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 43. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of ketamine by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism but decreases its levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 45. Ketoconazole increases efavirenz levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 46. Efavirenz and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 47. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of lansoprazole and lapatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Efavirenz and lapatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 48. Efavirenz and lasmiditan both increase sedation. Co-administration with other CNS depressants, including alcohol, has not been evaluated. Use caution and monitor. 49. Lemborexant decreases efavirenz levels by affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. Monitor CYP2B6 substrates for adequate clinical response and consider dose adjustments. Use caution and monitor. 50. Letermovir increases efavirenz levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 51. Efavirenz and leuprolide both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 52. Efavirenz and levalbuterol both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 53. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor blood pressure closely when co-administered with CYP3A4 inducers. 54. Efavirenz and levetiracetam both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 55. Efavirenz and levocetirizine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 56. Efavirenz and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 57. Levoketoconazole increases efavirenz levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 58. Efavirenz decreases the levels of levonorgestrel (intrauterine and oral) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Use alternative or backup contraception for 28 days after discontinuing enzyme inducers. 59. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of linagliptin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 60. Efavirenz and lithium both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 61. Efavirenz and loperamide both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 62. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 63. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of loratadine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 64. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of losartan by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism but decreases its levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 65. Lumacaftor may induce and ivacaftor may inhibit CYP2B6 substrates. Use caution and monitor. 66. Efavirenz and lumateperone both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 67. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of lurasidone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 68. Efavirenz and maprotiline both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 69. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
